newsitem.title: CANADA: Arakis says brokerage retracts report.
newsitem.headline: Arakis says brokerage retracts report.

text.p: Arakis Energy Corp said on Monday that investment house Schroder Wertheim retracted a report on the company's recently announced Sudan oil deal that Arakis said included factual errors.
Arakis said Schroder Wertheim clarified three errors made in the December 17 "Morning Meeting Highlight" report.
It said the brokerage has confirmed that Chevron Corp, the previous operator of Arakis's Heglig and Unity oil fields in southern Sudan, had no current claim on the concession.

Arakis said it informed Schroder Wertheim that its wholly owned subsidiary State Petroleum Corp -- not the Sudan government, as suggested in the report -- would continue as operator of the concession until replaced by a joint operating company in which state would participate.

Also, the piece said that the United States had granted aid of "$200 million of surplus weapons" to frontline African states Eritrea, Ethiopia and Uganda. However, the amount was a typographical error and should have read $20 million in military aid, Arakis said.
Earlier this month, Arakis announced a long-awaited $1-billion deal to form a consortium that would develop its oil concession and build a pipeline to the Red Sea from southern Sudan.
The partners include Arakis, China National Petroleum Corp, Malysia state oil company Petronas and the Sudan government.

An official with China's CNPC has told Reuters the state company expected stepped-up exploration of the concession to start in the New Year. Arakis has said it set a target for over 20 wells to be drilled in 1997 using four rigs. ((-- Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
